I like the place, it's one of those local places you wish was doing good, but I can't help but complain about how dirty and unkempt the fish tanks are. It's deplorable... dead fish, dirty walls, employees standing around doing nothing? There should be a baseline policy: If you are not doing anything, GO CLEAN THE TANKS! There is ich present (I've heard this from others here too), and too many dead fish.

The prices are pretty good, comparable to Petco and Petsmart (ie. less expensive than Monster Pets!), however, I just can't support a place that seems to care nothing about their fish.

Please clean your tanks. It's not like it's that hard. Take out dead fish, twice a day. Scrap the glass, and scrub... once a week. Go through and siphon out waste, and pick out dead plants, once a week. Then... keep the water changes going until the whole place is cleaner. Do I need to tell you how to run a fish store?

No other complains. Except maybe your employees could be a little more cordial, instead of pretending to be.

Extremely rude and unprofessional management. I called on behalf of a small high school to inquire about a possible donation for our upcoming science fair. Mid-conversation, I was abruptly told, “Put something in the mail, I don’t talk to people on the phone,” and then the call was disconnected. There was no attempt to answer my question or provide basic courtesy. Very disappointing experience, especially when simply reaching out for community support.

Visited on Christmas Eve more to have a look around and explore. This place feels nice, its clearly run with passion and care. Greeted with a warm hello upon entry but not chased around with "can I help". I ended up buying some Chili Rasbora (Not a fish I'd found anywhere else!) and cherry shrimp, I also had a number of fishkeeping questions varying in technicality. I was walked around the store to talk about various products that would solve my issues but in no way did it feel like a sales pitch. This was just two people enjoying a discussion about a field they share an interest in.

Its a little out of the way for me but I'll happily drive past both my local PetCo and PetSmart to revisit this wonderful little store.

As someone who enjoys aquariums; I enjoy this store. They got a wide variety of fresh water fish, shrimp, and some live plants as well. Also lots of accessories like drift and spider wood, all kinds of rocks, and so on. I’ll be visiting this store occasionally.

This shop was recommended to me by others in the area when I was looking for an axolotl for a birthday present for my best friend. I went to the shop last Friday 12/12 and purchased one. The staff was very nice and knowledgeable and in between buying the axolotl and giving it as a gift we did exactly what they said. Unfortunately, the axolotl was deceased by Sunday night. I understand these things happen so I called trying to get a refund and explained what happened and was told the best they could do was give me store credit or replace the axolotl. My friend lives states away, I have no way to get him a replacement. I don’t have other pets so a store credit would never get used. I am a business owner myself and understand that we have policies in place but when a $156 trip to a store results in a dead pet 2 days later, I was just hoping for more understanding and compassion.

Came to WWA looking for some information on any potential compatible fish to go into a tank with a Male Betta.  A guy came back to ask if we needed help, I explained briefly what I was looking for.  He was  a bit snobbish in his demeanor while pointing to the tanks on the one side, He points at the wall and said "Any of those over there, their the community fish."  I was thinking to myself "okay what does that mean to me, about what I was actually looking specifically for! For something that might do a bit of clean up in the tank too. He walked away, and then another guy came in to ask if we had any questions,  or needed help.   Out of no where, the original rude other guy came out and  basically interjected himself back into the conversation again with us. That's when the other (chill) guy said "Good Luck with your Betta!" I really want to like this place but have some reservations based on my visit there:

Pros:
- they have a wide selection of fish and can order others for you if they don’t currently have them in stock
- nice selection of aquatic plants and other products, with reasonable prices
- employees were very chill, friendly, and helpful

Cons:
- bought some frogbit which turned out to be infested with aphids. Was not a nice surprise to come home to… great reminder to always bleach/peroxide/alum dip your plants before adding them into your main tank
- they do not know whether the fish they get from their supplier are wild-caught or tank bred. This is kinda important because wild caught fish are more likely to carry parasites and imo should be medicated preventatively during quarantine, not just observed for 4 weeks. Additionally, if you care about conservation and sourcing fish responsibly, you can’t make an informed decision on whether to buy or not.
- on a similar note, they do not hold back new fish arrivals in quarantine or under observation before selling. This + the above means that when you buy fish from here, you have no way of really knowing whether they are coming into your tank with any parasites that are incubating in their systems, and since you can’t know whether they are wildcaught, or came into contact with wildcaught fish since the shop’s tanks house multiple species, you basically have to medicate all the fish you might buy from here.
